finding: premerge-check accepts the stored list mutants without a check that it belongs to the code it reruns. mutation_rerun_result takes the exit code from the rerun at the branch head and the list from .current-work/mutation-testing/<story-id>.json, but it compares neither a commit, the story_id field, nor the number of survivors. A list written for an earlier head, whose survivors are all resolved, therefore passes a rerun that fails on new survivors or on a crash of the mutation tool. The documented flow closes most of this path, because each run of the gate-check step rewrites the file without mutants, and the implementation agent writes the list after the last run. premerge-check is meant as an independent second gate, though, and here it trusts the gate-check step. The interface contract does not say which file it reads, as row 1 of spec-feedback-ST-0423.md records. The smallest fix has two parts. The gate-check step writes branch_head into the stored result, and mutation_rerun_result fails when branch_head is not the head of the story branch or story_id is not the story.
why_this_severity: The code exists only on the feature branch, and the gate is off in this repository (no to in_use). The story's Analysis prescribes the stored list, and each gate-check run rewrites the file, so a stale list needs a skipped step (no to fails_purpose). Until the fix, the dispatcher must make sure that the list it writes comes from the last run.
